concept: JetUP explainer #8, 'Getting your money out', for How it works 'Withdrawals', check 5 of the 5 Checks and the FAQ. 16:9, 1920x1080, 25 fps, captions burned in, the JetUP logo disc (never MTG's photo), the series' glass style, only the four signature sounds. It answers the visitor's own question, 'Can I get my money out?', with one South African picture built piece by piece: a fruit tree in your own backyard (spoken 'fruit tree', drawn as a mango). The backyard behind its gate ('TAG Markets · the broker') is your account at TAG Markets in your own name, the tree is your own money, and the fruit is your profit, when the strategy makes one, which you can pick any time. The promo is a gift branch tied onto your own tree (the $100 bonus comes with your own $100): the bonus is released after 12 months, and taking your own money out before then ends the promo, said once in MTG's recorded words and shown in the site's positive wording ('keep your own money in for 12 months to keep the promo'). Your basket outside the gate is your own crypto wallet: withdrawals go through the broker, to your wallet address, on the same network on both sides, about 48 hours on average per JetUP's one-pager, with the chip 'Fees and limits: the broker's terms'. The route names no wallet inside TAG Markets until MTG confirms how Sonic AI profits come out. Nothing is picked before the rule that matters, all in MTG's recorded voice: start small, do a small withdrawal early (the small mango from the hook is the first fruit picked), let the system prove itself, don't take my word for it, log in yourself and see your own balance, over his real, masked TAG Markets screen. A warm picture-first recap, 'Simple, right? Now it's your turn', tap any Join JetUP button, the fixed signature ending and 'Next: step-by-step, part 1'. Voice: 9 recorded body lines and the 4 shared lines (0 credits) plus 10 short new lines in MTG Master Voice V3 (683 characters, one request, 1 credit; 48 at the last record, 12 Nov 2026; only after MTG approves). Body about 78 s (75 to 86 s), total about 2:12 (2:09 to 2:20). Plan only: nothing is recorded, rendered or published.
picture: A fruit tree in your own backyard (spoken 'a fruit tree', drawn as a mango tree), built one piece at a time, each part keeping its colour and label in every scene. The backyard behind a gate signed 'TAG Markets · the broker', with your name plate on the gate = your account at TAG Markets, in your own name. The tree (trunk) = your own money. The fruit = your profit, when the tree bears some (there is profit only when the strategy makes one, so two or three mangoes ripen under one label, never a counting run or a laden tree). Ripe fruit you can pick whenever you like (a hand reaches up, ready to pick) = profits can be withdrawn any time. A gift branch with a lime ribbon tied onto your own tree = the Dennis Fast Start Promo's $100 bonus, which comes with your own $100 in the promo account (new partners, once). It is released after 12 months; because the gift grows on your own tree, you let the tree stand 12 months to keep the promo: keep your own money in for 12 months to keep the promo, and taking your own money out before then ends it. Your basket outside the gate = your own crypto wallet (for example your BIX wallet). The path from your backyard through the gate to your basket = withdrawals go through the broker, to your wallet address; the matching 'Network' badge at both ends = the same network on both sides, so your funds arrive safely; the clock chip = about 48 hours on average, JetUP's one-pager; the chip beside it = fees and limits are the broker's terms. This step is shown as the real thing (a labelled illustration: your account at TAG Markets, the broker, your crypto wallet), not forced into the tree, and it names no wallet inside TAG Markets. The one small mango that glowed behind the gate in the hook, the first fruit picked and the first to travel the path = start small and test a small withdrawal early: let the system prove itself to you. Nothing is picked before it. A key turning in your own name plate = don't take my word for it: log in yourself and see your own balance. The voice says only 'fruit', so the drawing can be a peach tree instead at no cost.
why_it_works:
1) It opens on the exact question every visitor has (the site's check 5 asks it), on screen from the first frame and in MTG's voice inside 5 seconds, and its loop ('the answer is growing in your own backyard') is paid off three seconds after the greeting. 2) One everyday South African picture, a fruit tree in the yard, makes visible what people mix up: profit (the fruit, pick it any time) and their own money (the tree). 3) The gift branch shows why the promo rule exists, not only what it is: the $100 bonus comes with your own $100 (the promo page: 'your own $100 plus a $100 bonus open a Sonic AI account'), so you let your tree stand 12 months to keep the promo. The rule feels natural, is said once in MTG's recorded words, and needs no warning. 4) 'When it bears fruit' and the label 'Your profit, when the strategy makes one' keep profit honest without a loss line: two or three mangoes on one tick, never a running count or a laden tree. No balance is ever shown, and the only amount is the promo's $100, as on the site. 5) The basket gives the wallet a home inside the same picture, and the way out is said in the site's own words (withdrawals go through the broker, the same network on both sides, JetUP's 48 hours with its source, fees and limits are the broker's terms), labelled 'Illustration', with no invented screens, routes, networks, fees or amounts. 6) The trust close is all MTG's recorded voice (start small, a small withdrawal early, let the system prove itself, don't take my word for it, log in yourself) over his real, masked screen. It answers the old fear of the withdrawal that never came without ever saying it, and the small mango from the hook makes the very first trip: nothing is picked before it. 7) It converts: a warm three-card recap, 'Now it's your turn', one action with the button tapped on screen, and a Next chip that is the very next step (part 1, create your JetUP account). 8) It is cheap: 683 new characters, 1 credit; everything else is banked voice.

Pictures weighed and dropped: a stokvel (pooled money someone else holds, the opposite of an account in your own name); a parcel and courier (Draft C: its numbered stops invented a withdrawal order the facts do not give, re-taught #7's bus-rank stops, and courier tracking messages look like the scam texts many South Africans get); a shop till (too close to #3's market stall); a borehole and tap (no line between profit and your own money); a bakery, cow or hen (suggests daily, guaranteed output); a lay-by (runs backwards); a bank fixed deposit (suggests guaranteed interest). The fruit tree is the one where every piece is true and nothing is forced, and it is new to the series.

scenes.name: The fruit tree

scenes.name: The gift branch

A branch with a lime gift ribbon ties onto the trunk (whoosh, 🎁 pop), with a two-line tag: '+$100 bonus with your own $100' / 'Dennis Fast Start Promo · new partners, once'. scenes.name: Into your basket
scenes.what_we_see: About 36 to 55 s. On 'Into your own basket' a woven basket appears outside the gate in 3D, empty and waiting (pop, 🧺 pop): 'Your crypto wallet'. Then the real thing, with the corner label 'Illustration' until MTG's own screens exist: the card 'Your account at TAG Markets', a path through the gate 'TAG Markets · the broker', and the card 'Your crypto wallet (for example your BIX wallet)', the address as dots only. On 'same network on both sides' a 'Network' badge lights at each end in the same colour (tick, tick) and the path lights up, dotted, to 'Arrives safely ✓' (pop); no fruit travels yet. On 'forty-eight hours' a clock chip 'About 48 hours on average' with the source tag 'JetUP's one-pager' (⏱️ pop); on 'on average', once it has landed, a second chip at the series' readable chip size (about 34 px, like the cover chips): 'Fees and limits: the broker's terms' (tick). Both hold through a pause of about 1 s after the line, until the scene changes. No network names, no amounts, no invented screens.

scenes.name: One small fruit first
scenes.what_we_see: About 55 to 67 s: the rule that matters, in MTG's recorded voice. A 'My advice?' card with the JetUP disc (whoosh). The small mango that glowed behind the gate in the hook is the first fruit picked (click) and makes the first trip along the path into the basket, to a tick: 'Test a small withdrawal early' (✅ pop).
